text:
Darren Raddysh scored 22 goals for Tampa Bay last season. In Toronto, after the trade, he has one in 26 games, on 3.4 expected goals and 69 shots. A 1.4% shooting rate from a defenseman who lives near the net (Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile for home-plate chances last season) is not a skill change. It's a slump, and the chances say it should break.

The Leafs are leaning on him hard: almost 24 minutes a night, 11 power-play points, 18 points overall and a four-game point streak, all assists. The team around him is the harder story. Toronto went 0-8-1 in the nine games before beating the Islanders on Nov. 23, and Yahoo Sports asked whether he was surprised by how head coach Jim Hiller has used him.

Evolving-Hockey had him 15th among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season, so the talent is not in question. What to watch: the goals, and whether his usage holds if Toronto changes direction.
headline: Raddysh is getting the looks, not the goals
